name: workz

scripts.//test:functions: The functions/ suites run on bare node (no runner, no emulator, ~1s), so there is no reason for the release gate to skip them — they lock the integrity-scan and decision-log classifiers the nightly nets depend on.
scripts.//test:firestore: The rules + stateful-timer suites. `npm test` INCLUDES these files but they self-skip without FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST, so a plain run reports them as 'skipped' and a rules regression passes the gate silently. This is the run that actually exercises them.
scripts.test:firestore: node scripts/check-emulator-port.mjs && firebase emulators:exec --project demo-workz-timer --only firestore "vitest run src/integration/firestore --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism"
scripts.//test:all: Everything the release gate must see: unit + functions + emulator. Used by /ship.
scripts.test:all: npm run test && npm run test:functions && npm run test:firestore

//browserslist: Pins the support floor EXPLICITLY (was implicit before). autoprefixer reads this for CSS prefixing; vite.config.js build.target mirrors it for JS. Floor ~= the audience's oldest realistic devices (field-worker phones / older iPhones). Bump deliberately, not by accident.
